contentBlocks.text: Yesterday you described materials by their properties. Today let's use those properties to sort and classify a whole group of objects — a real science skill called classification.

Gather 6-8 small objects from around your home. Pick one property, like flexible vs. rigid, and sort every object into one of those two groups. Then try sorting the same objects using a different property, like hard vs. soft. Notice: the same object can be sorted differently depending on which property you're using!
You just did real scientific classification — sorting objects by chosen properties. Tomorrow we'll investigate why certain materials are chosen for certain jobs.

objectives: Sort a group of real objects into categories based on a chosen observable property
Recognize that the same set of objects can be classified differently depending on which property is used
materialsNeeded: 6-8 household objects for a hands-on sorting activity
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Gather 6-8 real objects together.
2. Choose one property (flexible/rigid) and sort all objects into two groups.
3. Re-sort the same objects using a different property (hard/soft) and compare the new groupings.
4. Discuss why the groupings changed.
5. Move to the worksheet: sort the listed materials by the property given.
6. Close by inventing one more sorting category together.
differentiationTips: Struggling: sort using just one property at a time, without the added complexity of re-sorting by a second property
Ready for more: sort the same objects by three or more different properties and compare all the groupings
For a visual learner, use actual physical piles/groups on a table rather than writing the sorting on paper
teacherGuide.answerKey: Sample answers will vary by the specific materials sorted — check that the classification is consistent with the chosen property and that the child can explain their reasoning.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Classifying materials by observable properties is a core Grade 2 physical-science practice, directly extending yesterday's property-description vocabulary into an actual scientific sorting investigation.

generationData.instructions: Sort each material as FLEXIBLE (bends easily) or RIGID (stays stiff).
